comparison: Both strongly support the core methodological innovation (C2, C3, C12, C165, C169). OpenEval emphasizes experimental data and biophysical modeling demonstrating dMRS can probe cerebellar development. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'this work clearly demonstrates the potential of diffusion-weighted MRS' with 'solid evidence' and 'innovative data acquisition.' Complete agreement on this foundational claim.

Perfect alignment on metabolite concentration findings (C82-C86). OpenEval notes spectroscopic data in Figure 3A-B with external validation from literature. Peer reviewers praise 'fairly good data quality despite complexity' and do not challenge metabolite measurements. Both accept the protracted tNAA increase in cerebellum as a key regional distinction.

Complete agreement on the U-shaped cerebellar development finding (C10, C11, C161-C164). OpenEval notes the unexpected pattern is validated by 3D reconstructions. Peer reviewers affirm 'non-monotonic branching evolution in the cerebellum, matching 3D representations of Purkinje cells.' Both accept this novel finding with validation strengthening credibility.

Full agreement on experimental design and methods (C170-C176). OpenEval describes the design as reasonable with appropriate protocols. Peer reviewers praise it as 'a large-scale dataset of high value' with 'diffusion-weighted MRS acquired longitudinally in neonates' despite inherent challenges. Both recognize the technical achievements.

Divergence in certainty level regarding taurine as cerebellar neuronal marker (C107-C110, C115, C120, C131, C166, C168). OpenEval finds the convergent evidence 'compelling' and marks as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledge the claim but rate as UNCERTAIN, citing fundamental limitation: 'Metabolite compartmentation in one cell type or the other has often been challenged and is currently impossible to validate in vivo.'

Agreement on thalamic taurine interpretation (C121-C123, C126, C129, C137-C138). OpenEval finds the compartment switching hypothesis justified by data showing opposite trends and immunohistochemistry. Peer reviewers do not explicitly challenge this, accepting it with appropriate caution, though subject to general metabolite compartmentation validation caveats.

Strong alignment on diffusion findings and regional differences (C5-C8, C87, C98). OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and dMRS sensitivity to microstructural changes. Peer reviewers affirm 'lower metabolite ADC with increasing age' and 'differential microstructure and complexification' observed non-invasively. Both accept the data quality and statistical analyses. Peer result also includes C103 not in OpenEval R4.

Agreement on biophysical modeling justification (C148-C153). OpenEval notes sound reasoning with RMSE validation and appropriate technical constraints. Peer reviewers explicitly praise 'advanced biophysical modelling' as 'a strong asset of the study, going beyond the more commonly used signal representation metrics.' Both view modeling approach as methodological strength. Peer result also includes C154.

Agreement on sphere fraction interpretation for cerebellum (C9, C89, C93-C95, C104-C105). OpenEval finds biophysical modeling results well-supported with proper statistical assessment. Peer reviewers affirm 'decreasing sphere fraction with age in cerebellum, reflecting dendritic tree development' and accept the biological interpretation. Peer result also includes C99 not in OpenEval R5.

Agreement on data quality limitations (C77, C88). OpenEval praises transparent reporting of P5 motion artifacts and segmentation issues. Peer reviewers accept these technical limitations as 'inherent to the nature of the study' and note authors addressed concerns 'convincingly.' Both view the honest limitation reporting positively. Peer result also includes C78.

Agreement on volumetric developmental context (C76-C81, C96-C97). OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of segmentation limitations with differential timelines clearly demonstrated. Peer reviewers accept this as validation, noting dMRS is 'instrumental in assessing microstructure in a cell-specific manner' compared to volumetric approaches. Both view volumetric data as important context.

Agreement on data quality achievements and marker reliability (C132-C136, C167-C168). OpenEval emphasizes CRLB data supporting taurine over tNAA/Glu at early timepoints. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'fairly good data quality despite complexity' and feasibility 'despite known technical challenges.' Both accept the reliability assessment, though peer result focuses on subset of claims (C133-C135, C167).

Agreement on biological interpretation framework (C99-C100, C111-C116 vs C4, C100, C147). OpenEval discusses fsphere interpretation with granular layer and Bergmann glia hypotheses. Peer reviewers affirm the conceptual advantage of biophysical modeling 'going beyond ADC' with accepted sphere fraction framework. Overlap on C100 with complementary claims addressing interpretation advantages.

Agreement on methodological advantages of dMRS (C144-C147 vs C4, C100, C147). OpenEval emphasizes distinction between concentration (density-dependent) and diffusion properties (density-independent). Peer reviewers affirm biophysical modeling advantages over 'commonly used signal representation metrics.' Both recognize conceptual framework superiority, with minimal claim overlap (C147).

Agreement on dMRS-dMRI alignment (C101-C103 vs broader diffusion findings). OpenEval contextualizes dMRS within dMRI literature with appropriate caveats about signal differences. Peer reviewers affirm the broader diffusion findings showing developmental trajectories. Minimal direct overlap (C103) but complementary perspectives on diffusion-based developmental assessment.

Minimal overlap on technical considerations (C117-C120 vs taurine marker claims). OpenEval discusses taurine's higher Dintra improving model fitting with sensitivity analysis. Peer result addresses taurine as cerebellar marker with compartmentation validation concerns. Only C120 shared, representing different analytical perspectives on taurine data.

Minimal overlap on modeling limitations (C154-C159 vs C148-C154). OpenEval emphasizes honest assessment of morphometric modeling constraints including poor Nbranch estimation. Peer result focuses on modeling justification and strengths. Only C154 shared, representing complementary perspectives on modeling approach.

OpenEval addresses translational potential and comparative biology (C139-C143) with citations to human/primate studies and balanced discussion of challenges. No corresponding peer review evaluation found explicitly addressing cross-species translation or clinical applicability.

OpenEval addresses white matter handling with powder-averaging approach (C160) and fsphere expectations in oriented structures. No corresponding peer review evaluation found explicitly discussing white matter confounds or analytical approaches for anisotropic regions.

Peer reviewers express uncertainty about metabolite compartmentation assumptions (C59-C62), noting 'Metabolite compartmentation in one cell type or the other has often been challenged and is currently impossible to validate in vivo.' This foundational concern about cell-type specificity is not addressed as a separate evaluation in OpenEval results, though related to interpretations in R7 and R8.
